directions.name: Graphite and Signal
directions.summary: White and graphite with one signal blue for links and focus.
directions.curation: The common shape of serious software, done carefully: one neutral pair and a single interactive color.

reasoning.claim: Graphite reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Paper White, which suits dense tables and long sessions.
Signal Blue holds 3% of the declared area, so it always means "you can act here".

directions.watch_out: Easy to make indistinguishable from every other product. Brand character has to come from type and layout.
directions.choose_if: this is a working software interface where data and actions must stand out from a quiet UI
do: Reserve Signal Blue for links, focus and the primary action.
avoid: Do not use Signal Blue decoratively.

directions.name: Ultramarine Field
directions.summary: A saturated ultramarine ground carrying white type: the color is the brand.
directions.curation: A background-led identity where one saturated field does the work that a logo color usually does.

reasoning.claim: Cloud reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Ultramarine, so the field can hold text directly.
A whole field of color is memorable at a glance, which suits a product launch or a marketing site more than a dense interface.

directions.watch_out: Large saturated fields tire the eye in a product interface. Use a neutral variant inside the app.
directions.choose_if: a marketing site or launch needs one memorable color field rather than a quiet interface
do: Let the field fill whole sections.
avoid: Do not place photography directly on the field without a frame.

directions.name: Kelly Sheet
directions.summary: Plain white with a clear kelly green: friendly and direct.
directions.curation: A light, consumer-facing option with one bright color that stays readable at large sizes.

reasoning.claim: Kelly Green reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Sheet White, so it suits large type, icons and illustration.
One bright color on white feels approachable and simple, which suits consumer apps.

directions.watch_out: Kelly Green is too light for body text and small labels on white.
directions.choose_if: a consumer app should feel friendly and simple, with color in illustration and large type only
do: Use the derived text color for all reading text.
avoid: Do not set links in Kelly Green at small sizes.

directions.name: Bottle Green Ledger
directions.summary: Cream ledger paper with a bottle green: established and calm.
directions.curation: A traditional banking language, kept muted, for institutions that want trust through restraint rather than brightness.

reasoning.claim: Bottle Green reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Ledger Cream, so it carries headings and navigation.
A muted green on cream reads as established. It follows category convention, so it differentiates little.

directions.watch_out: This follows a category convention, so check the nearest competitors before choosing it.
directions.choose_if: an established financial or professional firm should signal trust through restraint
do: Use Bottle Green for structure: navigation, headings and rules.
avoid: Do not add gold to signal premium.

directions.name: Mint Ledger
directions.summary: A pale mint ground with deep navy: fresh, numerate and calm.
directions.curation: A two-color fintech identity where the tinted ground does as much work as the figure.

reasoning.claim: Deep Navy reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Mint Wash, so the pair carries all text.
A colored ground makes a finance brand recognisable without bright accents.

directions.watch_out: Mint grounds can look clinical in photography-heavy layouts.
directions.choose_if: a fintech or SaaS brand wants a recognisable tinted ground instead of a bright accent
do: Use Mint Wash as the main ground, not just a panel color.
avoid: Do not add a bright green for "money".

directions.name: Tangerine Wallet
directions.summary: A tangerine ground with ink navy: warm, bold and consumer-friendly.
directions.curation: A bold consumer fintech option that departs from the usual blue, built as two strong colors. Classification note (Phase 2 D6): Tangerine is a chromatic mid-tone ground (L 0.70, C 0.18) at the top of the 0.50–0.70 review band, where award chromatic colors peak, so its Light foundation is the least certain kind of call. Colors unchanged.

reasoning.claim: Ink Navy reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Tangerine, so text can sit directly on the color.
A warm ground makes a money app feel approachable and stands apart from blue category norms.

directions.watch_out: A warm, saturated ground is tiring in long sessions. Use it for marketing, not account screens.
directions.choose_if: a consumer finance or commerce brand wants to look warm and stand apart from blue competitors
do: Use Tangerine for marketing and key moments.
avoid: Do not use Tangerine for error or warning states.

directions.name: Phosphor
directions.summary: Carbon black with an electric phosphor lime.
directions.curation: An energetic dark option that keeps the bright color scarce, so it reads as light rather than as decoration.

reasoning.claim: Phosphor Lime reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Carbon, so it can carry labels and numbers.
A single electric color on near-black feels charged and technical.

directions.watch_out: Lime on black is a common esports cliché. The scarcity is what keeps it sharp.
directions.choose_if: a gaming, esports or technical brand wants an electric highlight on near-black, used sparingly
do: Keep Phosphor Lime under a tenth of the page.
avoid: Do not add glow or neon gradients.

directions.name: Slate Press
directions.summary: Blue-black slate with cold paper type: a tinted dark neutral for technical products that should not look like a default dark mode.
directions.curation: A dark neutral that leans cool instead of going to black. 30% of exact award neutrals carry a visible tint (research/report.md); the library's dark neutrals were all achromatic or warm.

reasoning.claim: Cold Paper reaches {ratio:figure/ground} on Slate Night, which suits dense tables and long sessions.
The cool cast reads as chosen rather than default while staying quiet enough for data-heavy screens.

directions.watch_out: The direction has no accent, so status colors must be chosen and checked against Slate Night separately.
directions.choose_if: a technical product wants a dark interface with a cool, deliberate cast rather than pure black
do: Step surfaces up in lightness from Slate Night rather than adding new hues.
avoid: Do not swap Slate Night for pure black; the tint is the identity.
